title: A randomized controlled study to assess the efficacy of topical Sinecathechins used as adjuvant therapy to topical ablative trichloroacetic acid in the Treatment of anal High grade squamous intraepithelial lesion.
official: A randomized controlled study to assess the efficacy of topical Sinecathechins used as adjuvant therapy to topical ablative trichloroacetic acid in the Treatment of anal High grade squamous intraepithelial lesion
summary: Main objective: To describe the proportion of patients free of HSIL at 48 weeks of treatment, defined as a complete or partial response (regression from HSIL to normal or LSIL, respectively) and free of recurrence, with topical Sinecatechins 10% ointment used as adjuvant therapy to ablative treatment, compared with ablative treatment alone.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adults ≥ 18 years of age.
2. HIV-1 infected individuals
3. Individuals with biopsy-proven anal HSIL within 6 months prior to the study.
4. Voluntary signature of the informed consent.
5. Be able to understand and comply with protocol requirements, instructions, and restrictions.
6. Be likely to complete the study as planned.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Any disease or condition of the patient that, in the opinion of the investigator, is not suitable for participation in the study.
2. Individuals who have received prior anal HSIL treatment in the last 3 months.
3. Individuals with two or more recurrences of anal HSIL in the last 2 years.
4. Individuals unable to understand the study protocol or any other condition that in the opinion of the investigator may compromise compliance with the protocol.
